messages:
david: FYI customer in eu-west hitting driver install failures on their VPC hosts after kernel security patch. stack: RHEL-derived custom kernel 5.15 -> upgraded to 5.15.49. driver 535 installer errors out with 'nvidia: module taints kernel' and dkms: ERROR: cannot find kernel-headers for 5.15.49

carmen: can you paste the install logs and uname -r? also which installer they used (runfile vs package)? :eyes:

david: they used the .run installer (silent mode). uname -r from customer: `5.15.49-rt1-customer`. attached snippet from their bootstrap: 
```
DKMS: add completed.
Error! Bad return status for module build on kernel: 5.15.49-rt1-customer (x86_64)
Consult /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/535/build/make.log for more information.
make: *** [Makefile:XX: modules] Error 2
```

alice: sounds like kernel flavor mismatch (rt/rt-preempt or custom 'customer' suffix). DKMS can't find matching headers because distro packages put headers in different path. if they're using custom kernels, driver runfile will try to build kmod with system gcc matching kernel build. common fixes: install `kernel-headers-$(uname -r)` from their build pipeline or use a prebuilt module that matches their kernel.

ben: what's impact on our private fleet? is this customer-only or could our private images be affected by the kernel patch? :thinking:

david: isolated to customer's VPC hosts for now. they manage their nodes. but we need to update our support matrix docs: we currently list RHEL kernel 5.15 and 6.1 families but we don't call out custom RT or vendor kernels. customer claims we told them kernel 5.15 supported.

eve (customer-eng): customer very upset because their compliance process auto-applies kernel patch. they want scriptable remediation. asking for 1) detection script to warn on kmod mismatch 2) guidance to use containerized driver fallback or pin older kernel.

carmen: quick triage steps for them: `uname -r`, `rpm -q kernel-headers-$(uname -r) || apt-get install linux-headers-$(uname -r)`, `cat /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/535/build/make.log`, `lsmod | grep nvidia` — ask them to paste make.log and output.

david: I've got the make.log lines — it's failing at building against `gcc version 12.1` that wasn't used to build their kernel. mismatch in gcc flags in `scripts/Makefile`. suggests we either supply prebuilt module or advise building kernel headers with same toolchain.

alice: alternative: ship a user-space-only fallback for inference (run container with bundled driver + --no-kmod) that uses nvidia-container-runtime + vendor driver image. doesn't cover all perf cases but avoids outage. we should add that to Private runbook. :thumbsup:

ben: operational question — can we detect this across other Private customers automatically? we could run a lightweight probe during agent handshake: check `modinfo nvidia` vs `nvidia-smi` and verify kernel module version matches driver toolkit version. if mismatch, mark instance as "driver-kmod-mismatch" in console and notify customer and SE.

alice: agree. also add a small script for customer side: `if [ "$(modinfo -F vermagic nvidia | awk '{print $1}')" != "$(uname -r)" ]; then echo "KMOD mismatch"; fi` (rough example). include instructions for DKMS/headers and runfile vs package differences.

eve (customer-eng): they tested container fallback and it passes basic inference but 20% perf regression. customer wants SLA impact calc and cost for us to maintain prebuilt kmods for their kernel flavor.

david: pricing/ops note — building and storing prebuilt kmods per-customer kernel matrix would increase CI/infra cost significantly. need a policy decision: support only vendor kernels listed in matrix OR offer paid managed-compat add-on to build+host modules for customer kernels.

ben: put this up for product discussion but for now do triage playbook: 1) provide detection script (alice) 2) provide containerized fallback instructions (alice) 3) offer DKMS guide to compile locally (carmen) 4) flag customer in console (ben) — can we get these done today?

david: I'll patch support-matrix doc to call out "custom kernels and RT flavors not supported unless enrolled in managed-compat program" and link to triage steps. draft done, pushing to docs repo in 2h.

alice: I'll prepare a minimal detection script + example container image reference (`ghcr.io/redwood/nvidia-fallback:stable`) and a short runbook snippet.

carmen: I'll take customer comms and the DKMS instructions. will ask them to run `sudo apt-get install build-essential linux-headers-$(uname -r)` and re-run installer; if they can't, recommend container fallback.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment for `private-agent v1.18.3` blocked: 2 hosts reported "driver-kmod-mismatch" tag, halting rollout.

ben: good catch deploy-bot — we'll not roll the agent until we add detection to v1.18.4. adding ticket INFRA-3129 to backlog.

david: action items assigned: alice -> detection + fallback doc, carmen -> DKMS guide + customer comms, ben -> console flag + INFRA-3129, me -> support-matrix update. follow-up in #eng-infra standup tomorrow. :calendar:

eve (customer-eng): customer confirmed they can apply container fallback overnight. wants managed-compat quote. I'll coordinate with sales. :pray:

carmen: closing loop here for now — keep updates in thread and paste any make.log excerpts. thanks everyone.
